title: Singapore's President warns of AI's risk to employment for fresh graduates
source_used: Central Oregon Daily (carrying Reuters' text, reporting by Rae Wee; Reuters page returned HTTP 401), cross-read against The Economic Times
key_facts: Singapore President Tharman Shanmugaratnam spoke at the IMF and World Bank annual meetings in Bangkok on Monday 12 Oct 2026.
He said governments across the world should address how AI is dampening jobs demand for fresh graduates.
He said 'the first rung in employment, your first job upon graduation, is now seeing less demand' and called it a problem 'we have to address very soon'.
He said 'The evidence is already very clear, it's clearest in the most AI-exposed sectors.'
He said the world should also avoid a 'new divergence' between developing and advanced economies due to disruptions from AI.
The Reuters report gives no figures.
quote_evidence: "There is a particular problem that we have to address very soon... and that is that, the first rung in employment, your first job upon graduation, is now seeing less demand," Shanmugaratnam told IMF and World Bank annual meetings in Bangkok on Monday.
"The evidence is already very clear, it's clearest in the most AI-exposed sectors."
He said the world should also avoid a situation where a "new divergence" forms between developing and advanced economies due to disruptions from AI.
why_it_matters_hint: A head of state says AI is already reducing entry-level job demand for new graduates and that governments should act soon.
notes: Reuters original blocked (401); read Reuters' text on Central Oregon Daily and The Economic Times (both credit Reuters). Same Bangkok meetings as the IMF chief's warning (C05-01). No figures are given.
